public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 7

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture7

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 7](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$L_s(G) \ge \max_v \lambda(v) - 1 + n - 2 \alpha(G)$,
where $L_s(G)$ is the maximum number of leaves over all spanning trees of $G$,
$n = |V(G)|$, $\alpha(G) = G.\mathrm{indepNum}$ is the independence number, and
$\lambda(v) = \mathrm{indepNeighborsCard}\, G\, v$ is the independence number of the
neighbourhood of $v$.

Proved by DeLaVina, Fajtlowicz, Waller (2002).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture7 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    let maxL := (Finset.univ.image (fun v => indepNeighborsCard G v)).max' (by simp)
    ((maxL : ℤ) - 1 + (Fintype.card α : ℤ) - 2 * (G.indepNum : ℤ) : ℝ) ≤ Ls G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The independence number is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ G.indepNum := Nat.zero_le _

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture7

reformulations.difference: Lean assumes `[Nontrivial α]`, whereas the source states the bound for simple connected finite graphs without explicitly excluding the one-vertex graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness excludes the empty vertex type. For a one-vertex graph, the independence number is 1 and the maximum neighborhood independence number is 0, so the proposed lower bound is −2. Since the maximum leaf count is nonnegative, this case holds automatically. Consequently restricting to at least two vertices does not change the universal claim. In /workspace/review/leaf_checks.lean I proved the singleton case and the pointwise equivalence `(Nontrivial V → sourceInequality G) ↔ sourceInequality G`, without using the conjecture or any sorry.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaViña, Written on the Wall II, November 1996: definitions and Conjectures 2 and 7, including the remarks following Conjecture 7. Archived original list: http://web.archive.org/web/20230703190700/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII.pdf

Written on the Wall II website: introductory material, link identifying the original list of Conjectures 1–8, and reference [DFW]. http://web.archive.org/web/20241118002601/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/list.htm

E. DeLaViña and B. Waller, Spanning Trees with Many Leaves and Average Distance, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 15 (2008), R33: definitions on pp. 2–3, Theorem 7 on p. 4, and reference [14]. https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v15i1r33/pdf

Crossref bibliographic records, including DeLaViña–Fajtlowicz–Waller, On some conjectures of Griggs and graffiti, DOI 10.1090/dimacs/069/07: https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=DeLaVina%20Fajtlowicz%20Waller%20spanning%20trees&rows=5
review.notes: No mathematical defects found in the theorem or its sanity-check example. The live reference site was unavailable; its archived original list and the published paper both confirm the bound. The paper's Theorem 7 confirms the solved status. Inspected all relevant definitions and casts. Independent Lean proofs establish that Ls attains the maximum leaf count on connected finite graphs, is nonnegative, and equals 2 on K₂. Computable tests of independence numbers and exhaustive graph enumeration through four vertices found no discrepancies. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, leaf_checks.lean, and small_graphs.lean.
